_notes: Read functions for the OriginBI assessment platform.
Scope keys: corporate_account_id (B2B tenant), user_id (a student's own rows). ADMIN is exempt from both.

Every query is dedup-safe: the dev database is double-seeded (sessions, attempts, reports, corporate_accounts, aci_score_bands and groups all have exactly two physical rows per id, with no primary key). DISTINCT ON (id) and COUNT(DISTINCT id) make each function correct whether or not that is fixed.
An assessment level's id is NOT its level number: level 3 (IAT) is id 5 and level 4 (Metaphor) is id 3. Every level function joins assessment_levels and orders by sort_order rather than assuming.
Levels 1 (DISC) and 2 (ACI) carry a numeric score. Levels 3 (IAT) and 4 (Metaphor) do not — they are pattern-based, so their functions report completion and pattern detail, never a mark.
A candidate may retake a level. The per-level functions return the most recent attempt for each level, not every attempt.
Roles expected in the application: STUDENT, CORPORATE, ADMIN. Import this, create those roles, then take the functions live.

The two report actions are HTTP calls into student-service, not database writes. They need a service named "reports" registered on the Applications page, and the role must hold the "reports.generate" write scope. See docs/ORIGINBI_REPORT_SETUP.md.

The report endpoint is keyed on users.id, NOT registrations.id — find_candidate returns both, and generate_candidate_report takes the user id. Passing a registration id there would generate a different person's report.

functions.name: find_candidate
functions.description: Find one candidate (a registered person) within your company by their name, and return their assessment progress: which program, the status of their latest assessment session, and whether their report is ready. Accepts a full or partial name; when several people match, the agent asks which one.
whenToUse: what is the status of candidate Priya Sharma
is the report ready for Shreyas Santhosh
whenNotToUse: Not for listing everyone or counting candidates — use list_candidates or candidate_status_counts.
Not for a student asking about their own result — that is my_assessment_status.

name.description: The candidate's full or partial name, e.g. "Priya" or "Priya Sharma".

registration_id.description: The candidate's registration id. Only set this when resolving which candidate was meant after the agent has asked; normally search by name.

functions.sqlTemplate:
SELECT DISTINCT ON (r.id)
       r.id AS id,
       r.full_name AS label,
       coalesce(p.name, 'no program') || ' · ' || coalesce(s.status, 'no session yet') AS detail,
       CASE
         WHEN r.id = {{param:registration_id}} THEN 100
         WHEN lower(r.full_name) = lower({{param:name}}) THEN 100
         ELSE 70
       END AS match_score,
       r.full_name,
       r.user_id,
       coalesce(p.name, 'unassigned') AS program,
       r.status AS registration_status,
       coalesce(s.status, 'NO_SESSION') AS session_status,
       coalesce(s.is_report_ready, false) AS report_ready
  FROM registrations r
  LEFT JOIN programs p ON p.id = r.program_id
  LEFT JOIN assessment_sessions s ON s.registration_id = r.id
 WHERE r.is_deleted IS NOT TRUE
   AND (
        r.full_name ILIKE '%' || {{param:name}} || '%'
     OR r.id = {{param:registration_id}}
   )
   AND {{scope:corporate_account_id}}
 ORDER BY r.id, s.created_at DESC NULLS LAST

functions.name: list_candidates
functions.description: List the candidates registered under your company, each with their program and the status of their latest assessment session. Optionally filter to one session status. Returns many rows; for a single named person use find_candidate.
whenToUse: list everyone who has not started their assessment
which candidates are still in progress
whenNotToUse: Not for a single named person — use find_candidate.
Not for just the numbers by status — use candidate_status_counts.

session_status.description: Restrict to candidates whose latest session has this status. Leave unset for all.

functions.sqlTemplate:
SELECT DISTINCT ON (r.id)
       r.id,
       r.full_name,
       coalesce(p.name, 'unassigned') AS program,
       coalesce(s.status, 'NO_SESSION') AS session_status,
       coalesce(s.is_report_ready, false) AS report_ready,
       r.created_at
  FROM registrations r
  LEFT JOIN programs p ON p.id = r.program_id
  LEFT JOIN assessment_sessions s ON s.registration_id = r.id
 WHERE r.is_deleted IS NOT TRUE
   AND (cast({{param:session_status}} AS text) IS NULL OR coalesce(s.status, 'NO_SESSION') = {{param:session_status}})
   AND {{scope:corporate_account_id}}
 ORDER BY r.id, s.created_at DESC NULLS LAST

functions.name: candidate_status_counts
functions.description: Count your company's candidates grouped by the status of their latest assessment session (COMPLETED, IN_PROGRESS, EXPIRED, NOT_STARTED, and so on). Use this for "how many" questions rather than listing people.
whenToUse: how many candidates have completed the assessment
give me a breakdown of our candidates by status
whenNotToUse: Not for the actual names — use list_candidates.
Not for one person — use find_candidate.
functions.sqlTemplate:
SELECT coalesce(s.status, 'NO_SESSION') AS session_status,
       count(DISTINCT r.id) AS candidates
  FROM registrations r
  LEFT JOIN assessment_sessions s ON s.registration_id = r.id
 WHERE r.is_deleted IS NOT TRUE
   AND {{scope:corporate_account_id}}
 GROUP BY coalesce(s.status, 'NO_SESSION')
 ORDER BY candidates DESC

functions.name: corporate_credit_balance
functions.description: Show your company's assessment credit balance: how many credits are available now, how many were purchased in total, and whether the account is active.
whenToUse: how many credits do we have left
whenNotToUse: Not for candidates or assessments — this is only the credit balance.
functions.sqlTemplate:
SELECT DISTINCT ON (ca.id)
       ca.id,
       ca.company_name,
       ca.available_credits,
       ca.total_credits,
       ca.is_active
  FROM corporate_accounts ca
 WHERE {{scope:corporate_account_id}}
 ORDER BY ca.id

functions.name: find_corporate_account
functions.description: Administrator lookup of a corporate (company) account by company name, returning its credit balance and whether it is active. When several companies match, the agent asks which one.
whenToUse: look up the corporate account for Touchmark
whenNotToUse: Not for a candidate or a person — use find_user or find_candidate.
Available to administrators only.

company_name.description: Full or partial company name, e.g. "Touchmark".

corporate_account_id.description: The corporate account id. Set only when resolving which company was meant after the agent asked.

functions.sqlTemplate:
SELECT DISTINCT ON (ca.id)
       ca.id AS id,
       ca.company_name AS label,
       ca.available_credits::text || ' of ' || ca.total_credits::text || ' credits left' AS detail,
       CASE
         WHEN ca.id = {{param:corporate_account_id}} THEN 100
         WHEN lower(ca.company_name) = lower({{param:company_name}}) THEN 100
         ELSE 70
       END AS match_score,
       ca.company_name,
       ca.available_credits,
       ca.total_credits,
       ca.is_active
  FROM corporate_accounts ca
 WHERE ca.company_name ILIKE '%' || {{param:company_name}} || '%'
    OR ca.id = {{param:corporate_account_id}}
 ORDER BY ca.id

functions.name: find_user
functions.description: Administrator lookup of a platform user by email address, returning their role (STUDENT, CORPORATE, AFFILIATE, ADMIN) and whether the account is active or blocked. When several emails match a partial search, the agent asks which one.
whenToUse: find the user with email jane@example.com
whenNotToUse: Not for a candidate's assessment progress — use find_candidate.
Available to administrators only.

user_id.description: The user id. Set only when resolving which user was meant after the agent asked.

functions.sqlTemplate:
SELECT DISTINCT ON (u.id)
       u.id AS id,
       u.email AS label,
       u.role || ' · ' || CASE WHEN u.is_blocked THEN 'blocked' WHEN u.is_active THEN 'active' ELSE 'inactive' END AS detail,
       CASE
         WHEN u.id = {{param:user_id}} THEN 100
         WHEN lower(u.email) = lower({{param:email}}) THEN 100
         ELSE 70
       END AS match_score,
       u.email,
       u.role,
       u.is_active,
       u.is_blocked,
       u.corporate_id
  FROM users u
 WHERE u.email ILIKE '%' || {{param:email}} || '%'
    OR u.id = {{param:user_id}}
 ORDER BY u.id

functions.name: platform_assessment_overview
functions.description: Administrator platform-wide count of assessment sessions grouped by status (COMPLETED, IN_PROGRESS, EXPIRED, and so on), across every company and student. Use for a health-of-the-platform overview.
whenToUse: how many assessments have been completed across the platform
give me a platform-wide assessment breakdown
how many sessions are in progress overall
whenNotToUse: Not scoped to one company — for that use candidate_status_counts as that company.
Available to administrators only.
functions.sqlTemplate:
SELECT coalesce(s.status, 'NO_SESSION') AS session_status,
       count(DISTINCT s.id) AS sessions
  FROM assessment_sessions s
 GROUP BY coalesce(s.status, 'NO_SESSION')
 ORDER BY sessions DESC

functions.name: my_registration_status
functions.description: For the signed-in student: their own registration details — their name, the program they registered for, the registration status, payment status, and whether AI counsellor access is enabled. Returns only the caller's own records.
whenToUse: do I have AI counsellor access
whenNotToUse: Not for assessment progress or reports — use my_assessment_status or my_report.
Only ever returns the caller's own data.
functions.sqlTemplate:
SELECT DISTINCT ON (r.id)
       r.id,
       r.full_name,
       coalesce(p.name, 'unassigned') AS program,
       r.status AS registration_status,
       coalesce(r.payment_status, 'NONE') AS payment_status,
       coalesce(r.has_ai_counsellor, false) AS ai_counsellor,
       r.gender,
       r.mobile_number,
       r.created_at
  FROM registrations r
  LEFT JOIN programs p ON p.id = r.program_id
 WHERE r.is_deleted IS NOT TRUE
   AND {{scope:user_id}}
 ORDER BY r.id DESC

functions.name: my_assessment_status
functions.description: For the signed-in student: the status of their own assessment session(s) — which program, whether it is completed, in progress or expired, and whether the report is ready. Returns only the caller's own records.
whenToUse: what is the status of my assessment
is my assessment still in progress
whenNotToUse: Not for the report itself — use my_report.
Only ever returns the caller's own data.
functions.sqlTemplate:
SELECT DISTINCT ON (s.id)
       s.id,
       r.full_name,
       coalesce(p.name, 'unassigned') AS program,
       s.status AS session_status,
       coalesce(s.is_report_ready, false) AS report_ready,
       s.completed_at,
       s.created_at
  FROM assessment_sessions s
  LEFT JOIN programs p ON p.id = s.program_id
  LEFT JOIN registrations r ON r.id = s.registration_id
 WHERE {{scope:user_id}}
 ORDER BY s.id DESC

functions.name: my_report
functions.description: For the signed-in student: their own assessment report(s), showing the report number, the program, when it was generated, and whether a downloadable report is available. Returns only the caller's own records.
whenNotToUse: Not for whether the assessment itself is finished — use my_assessment_status.
Only ever returns the caller's own data.
functions.sqlTemplate:
SELECT DISTINCT ON (ar.id)
       ar.id,
       ar.report_number,
       (ar.report_url IS NOT NULL) AS report_available,
       ar.generated_at,
       coalesce(p.name, 'unassigned') AS program
  FROM assessment_reports ar
  JOIN assessment_sessions s ON s.id = ar.assessment_session_id
  LEFT JOIN programs p ON p.id = s.program_id
 WHERE {{scope:user_id}}
 ORDER BY ar.id DESC

functions.name: my_level_scores
functions.description: For the signed-in student: their result at every assessment level, one row per level in order — the level name, what it measures, whether it is completed, the score out of the maximum with a percentage, and when it was finished. Levels 1 and 2 carry a numeric score; levels 3 and 4 are pattern-based and show completion rather than a mark.
whenToUse: how did I do in each level
what did I get for level 2
whenNotToUse: Not for the D/I/S/C breakdown of level 1 — that is my_behavioural_profile.
Not for the five agile values behind the level 2 total — that is my_agile_index.
Only ever returns the caller's own data.
functions.sqlTemplate:
SELECT DISTINCT ON (l.sort_order)
       l.level_number,
       l.name AS level,
       l.pattern_type AS measures,
       a.status,
       a.total_score AS score,
       nullif(coalesce(nullif(a.max_score_snapshot, 0), l.max_score), 0) AS out_of,
       round(100.0 * a.total_score
             / nullif(coalesce(nullif(a.max_score_snapshot, 0), l.max_score), 0), 1) AS percent,
       a.sincerity_class,
       pt.blended_style_name AS dominant_style,
       a.started_at,
       a.completed_at
  FROM assessment_attempts a
  JOIN assessment_levels l ON l.id = a.assessment_level_id
  LEFT JOIN personality_traits pt ON pt.id = a.dominant_trait_id
 WHERE {{scope:user_id}}
 ORDER BY l.sort_order, a.completed_at DESC NULLS LAST, a.id DESC

functions.name: my_behavioural_profile
functions.description: For the signed-in student: the level 1 behavioural breakdown — their Dominance, Influence, Steadiness and Compliance scores, the total, and the blended style those four produce (such as "Creative Thinker") with what that style means.
whenToUse: what are my dominance and influence scores
whenNotToUse: Not for every level at once — that is my_level_scores.
Not for the agile values from level 2 — that is my_agile_index.
Only ever returns the caller's own data.
functions.sqlTemplate:
SELECT DISTINCT ON (ar.id)
       ar.report_number,
       (ar.disc_scores->>'D')::numeric AS dominance,
       (ar.disc_scores->>'I')::numeric AS influence,
       (ar.disc_scores->>'S')::numeric AS steadiness,
       (ar.disc_scores->>'C')::numeric AS compliance,
       (ar.disc_scores->>'total')::numeric AS total,
       pt.blended_style_name AS style,
       pt.blended_style_desc AS what_the_style_means,
       ar.overall_sincerity,
       ar.generated_at
  FROM assessment_reports ar
  JOIN assessment_sessions s ON s.id = ar.assessment_session_id
  LEFT JOIN personality_traits pt ON pt.id = ar.dominant_trait_id
 WHERE ar.disc_scores IS NOT NULL AND ar.disc_scores <> '{}'::jsonb
   AND {{scope:user_id}}
 ORDER BY ar.id DESC

functions.name: my_agile_index
functions.description: For the signed-in student: the level 2 Agile Compatibility Index — their Commitment, Focus, Openness, Respect and Courage scores, the total, and which band that total falls in (Agile Naturalist, Adaptive, Learner or Resistant) with the interpretation of that band.
whenToUse: how did I do on commitment and courage
whenNotToUse: Not for the DISC letters — that is my_behavioural_profile.
Not for every level at once — that is my_level_scores.
Only ever returns the caller's own data.
functions.sqlTemplate:
SELECT DISTINCT ON (ar.id)
       (ar.agile_scores->>'Commitment')::numeric AS commitment,
       (ar.agile_scores->>'Focus')::numeric      AS focus,
       (ar.agile_scores->>'Openness')::numeric   AS openness,
       (ar.agile_scores->>'Respect')::numeric    AS respect,
       (ar.agile_scores->>'Courage')::numeric    AS courage,
       (ar.agile_scores->>'total')::numeric      AS total,
       b.level_name AS band,
       b.compatibility_tag AS band_summary,
       b.interpretation AS what_the_band_means,
       ar.generated_at
  FROM assessment_reports ar
  JOIN assessment_sessions s ON s.id = ar.assessment_session_id
  LEFT JOIN aci_score_bands b
         ON b.is_active AND b.is_deleted IS NOT TRUE
        AND (ar.agile_scores->>'total')::numeric BETWEEN b.min_score AND b.max_score
 WHERE ar.agile_scores IS NOT NULL AND ar.agile_scores <> '{}'::jsonb
   AND {{scope:user_id}}
 ORDER BY ar.id DESC

functions.name: my_iat_patterns
functions.description: For the signed-in student: their level 3 association-test result, one row per comparison. Each row gives how much longer they took on one pairing than the other, whether that hesitation was low, moderate or strong, their error rate, and which pairing was the slower one.
whenNotToUse: Level 3 has no numeric score, so this is not a "what did I get" answer — for scores use my_level_scores.
Only ever returns the caller's own data.
functions.sqlTemplate:
SELECT DISTINCT ON (m.module_order, im.id)
       im.display_name AS comparison,
       m.pattern_label AS hesitation,
       round(m.speed_gap_ms) AS hesitation_ms,
       round(m.compatible_average_ms) AS faster_pairing_ms,
       round(m.incompatible_average_ms) AS slower_pairing_ms,
       round(m.error_rate, 1) AS error_percent,
       im.slowed_on_description AS slower_pairing_was,
       m.status,
       m.completed_at
  FROM iat_attempt_modules m
  JOIN iat_modules im ON im.id = m.module_id
 WHERE {{scope:user_id}}
 ORDER BY m.module_order, im.id, m.id DESC

functions.name: candidate_level_scores
functions.description: One candidate's result at every assessment level, one row per level in order — the level name, what it measures, status, score out of the maximum with a percentage, and when it was finished. Takes a registration id from find_candidate. Only returns candidates in your own company.
whenToUse: how did this candidate do in each level
show me the level breakdown for <candidate>
what did they get for level 1
whenNotToUse: Not for finding the candidate in the first place — use find_candidate, then this.
Not for the D/I/S/C or agile detail — those are candidate_behavioural_profile.
Not for a whole cohort — use level_completion_funnel.

registration_id.description: The candidate's registration id, as returned by find_candidate. Ask for the candidate by name first if you do not have it.

functions.sqlTemplate:
SELECT DISTINCT ON (l.sort_order)
       r.full_name AS candidate,
       l.level_number,
       l.name AS level,
       l.pattern_type AS measures,
       a.status,
       a.total_score AS score,
       nullif(coalesce(nullif(a.max_score_snapshot, 0), l.max_score), 0) AS out_of,
       round(100.0 * a.total_score
             / nullif(coalesce(nullif(a.max_score_snapshot, 0), l.max_score), 0), 1) AS percent,
       a.sincerity_class,
       pt.blended_style_name AS dominant_style,
       a.started_at,
       a.completed_at
  FROM assessment_attempts a
  JOIN registrations r ON r.id = a.registration_id
  JOIN assessment_levels l ON l.id = a.assessment_level_id
  LEFT JOIN personality_traits pt ON pt.id = a.dominant_trait_id
 WHERE r.is_deleted IS NOT TRUE
   AND a.registration_id = {{param:registration_id}}
   AND {{scope:corporate_account_id}}
 ORDER BY l.sort_order, a.completed_at DESC NULLS LAST, a.id DESC

functions.name: candidate_behavioural_profile
functions.description: One candidate's level 1 behavioural breakdown — Dominance, Influence, Steadiness and Compliance with the total, and the blended style those produce with what it means. Takes a registration id from find_candidate. Only returns candidates in your own company.
whenToUse: what is this candidate's DISC profile
show me the behavioural breakdown for <candidate>
whenNotToUse: Not for the agile values — that is candidate_agile_index.
Not for every level at once — that is candidate_level_scores.

registration_id.description: The candidate's registration id, as returned by find_candidate. Ask for the candidate by name first if you do not have it.

functions.sqlTemplate:
SELECT DISTINCT ON (ar.id)
       ar.report_number,
       (ar.disc_scores->>'D')::numeric AS dominance,
       (ar.disc_scores->>'I')::numeric AS influence,
       (ar.disc_scores->>'S')::numeric AS steadiness,
       (ar.disc_scores->>'C')::numeric AS compliance,
       (ar.disc_scores->>'total')::numeric AS total,
       pt.blended_style_name AS style,
       pt.blended_style_desc AS what_the_style_means,
       ar.overall_sincerity,
       ar.generated_at
  FROM assessment_reports ar

 WHERE ar.disc_scores IS NOT NULL AND ar.disc_scores <> '{}'::jsonb
   AND r.is_deleted IS NOT TRUE
   AND s.registration_id = {{param:registration_id}}
   AND {{scope:corporate_account_id}}
 ORDER BY ar.id DESC

functions.name: candidate_agile_index

whenToUse: what is this candidate's agile score
how did they score on openness and courage

Not for every level at once — that is candidate_level_scores.

registration_id.description: The candidate's registration id, as returned by find_candidate. Ask for the candidate by name first if you do not have it.

functions.sqlTemplate:
SELECT DISTINCT ON (ar.id)
       (ar.agile_scores->>'Commitment')::numeric AS commitment,
       (ar.agile_scores->>'Focus')::numeric      AS focus,
       (ar.agile_scores->>'Openness')::numeric   AS openness,
       (ar.agile_scores->>'Respect')::numeric    AS respect,

       b.level_name AS band,
       b.compatibility_tag AS band_summary,

  FROM assessment_reports ar

  JOIN registrations r ON r.id = s.registration_id
  LEFT JOIN aci_score_bands b
         ON b.is_active AND b.is_deleted IS NOT TRUE

functions.name: candidate_iat_patterns
functions.description: One candidate's level 3 association-test result, one row per comparison: how much longer they took on one pairing than the other, whether that hesitation was low, moderate or strong, the error rate, and which pairing was slower. Takes a registration id from find_candidate. Only returns candidates in your own company.
whenToUse: what did level 3 show for this candidate
show me the association patterns for <candidate>
whenNotToUse: Level 3 produces no numeric score — for scores use candidate_level_scores.

registration_id.description: The candidate's registration id, as returned by find_candidate. Ask for the candidate by name first if you do not have it.

functions.sqlTemplate:
SELECT DISTINCT ON (m.module_order, im.id)
       im.display_name AS comparison,
       m.pattern_label AS hesitation,
       round(m.speed_gap_ms) AS hesitation_ms,
       round(m.compatible_average_ms) AS faster_pairing_ms,
       round(m.incompatible_average_ms) AS slower_pairing_ms,
       round(m.error_rate, 1) AS error_percent,
       im.slowed_on_description AS slower_pairing_was,

  FROM iat_attempt_modules m
  JOIN iat_modules im ON im.id = m.module_id
  JOIN registrations r ON r.id = m.registration_id
 WHERE r.is_deleted IS NOT TRUE
   AND m.registration_id = {{param:registration_id}}
   AND {{scope:corporate_account_id}}
 ORDER BY m.module_order, im.id, m.id DESC

functions.name: level_completion_funnel
functions.description: How your company's candidates are distributed across the assessment levels: for each level reached, how many attempts are completed, in progress, not started or expired, how many distinct candidates it covers, and the average score of the completed ones. Shows where a cohort is stuck.
whenToUse: where are our candidates getting stuck
how many have finished each level
give me a level by level breakdown
what is the average score at level 2
whenNotToUse: Not for one candidate — use candidate_level_scores.
Not for overall session status — use candidate_status_counts.
A level no candidate has reached does not appear at all.
functions.sqlTemplate:
SELECT l.level_number,
       l.name AS level,
       l.pattern_type AS measures,
       count(DISTINCT a.id) FILTER (WHERE a.status = 'COMPLETED')   AS completed,
       count(DISTINCT a.id) FILTER (WHERE a.status = 'IN_PROGRESS') AS in_progress,
       count(DISTINCT a.id) FILTER (WHERE a.status = 'NOT_STARTED') AS not_started,
       count(DISTINCT a.id) FILTER (WHERE a.status IN ('EXPIRED', 'PARTIALLY_EXPIRED')) AS expired,
       count(DISTINCT a.registration_id) AS candidates,
       round(avg(a.total_score) FILTER (WHERE a.status = 'COMPLETED'), 1) AS average_score
  FROM assessment_attempts a
  JOIN registrations r ON r.id = a.registration_id
  JOIN assessment_levels l ON l.id = a.assessment_level_id
 WHERE r.is_deleted IS NOT TRUE
   AND {{scope:corporate_account_id}}
 GROUP BY l.level_number, l.name, l.pattern_type, l.sort_order
 ORDER BY l.sort_order

functions.name: attempts_expiring_soon
functions.description: Candidates in your company whose current assessment level has a deadline coming up and is not finished, soonest first, with how many hours are left. Use this to chase people before they run out of time.
whenToUse: who is about to run out of time
anything expiring in the next 48 hours
whenNotToUse: Not for deadlines that have already passed — that is stalled_attempts.
Not for one candidate — use candidate_level_scores.

within_hours.description: How far ahead to look, in hours. Defaults to 72 (three days).

functions.sqlTemplate:
SELECT DISTINCT ON (a.id)
       r.full_name AS candidate,
       l.level_number,
       l.name AS level,
       a.status,
       coalesce(a.must_finish_by, a.expires_at) AS deadline,
       round(extract(epoch FROM coalesce(a.must_finish_by, a.expires_at) - now()) / 3600) AS hours_left
  FROM assessment_attempts a
  JOIN registrations r ON r.id = a.registration_id
  JOIN assessment_levels l ON l.id = a.assessment_level_id
 WHERE r.is_deleted IS NOT TRUE
   AND a.status IN ('NOT_STARTED', 'IN_PROGRESS', 'PARTIALLY_EXPIRED')
   AND coalesce(a.must_finish_by, a.expires_at)
       BETWEEN now() AND now() + make_interval(hours => coalesce({{param:within_hours}}::int, 72))
   AND {{scope:corporate_account_id}}
 ORDER BY a.id, deadline

functions.name: stalled_attempts
functions.description: Candidates in your company whose deadline for a level has already passed without them finishing it, most overdue first, with how many days ago the deadline was. These are the people who need a new window rather than a reminder.
whenToUse: who has run out of time
which assessments expired without being finished
whenNotToUse: Not for deadlines still in the future — that is attempts_expiring_soon.
Not for a status breakdown — use candidate_status_counts.
functions.sqlTemplate:
SELECT DISTINCT ON (a.id)
       r.full_name AS candidate,
       l.level_number,
       l.name AS level,
       a.status,
       coalesce(a.must_finish_by, a.expires_at) AS deadline_was,
       round(extract(epoch FROM now() - coalesce(a.must_finish_by, a.expires_at)) / 86400) AS days_overdue
  FROM assessment_attempts a
  JOIN registrations r ON r.id = a.registration_id
  JOIN assessment_levels l ON l.id = a.assessment_level_id
 WHERE r.is_deleted IS NOT TRUE
   AND a.status <> 'COMPLETED'
   AND coalesce(a.must_finish_by, a.expires_at) < now()
   AND {{scope:corporate_account_id}}
 ORDER BY a.id, deadline_was

functions.name: corporate_credit_history
functions.description: Your company's assessment credit movements, most recent first: whether each entry added (CREDIT) or used (DEBIT) credits, how many, the reason, and the amount and payment status where one applies. Use this for "where did our credits go"; for the number remaining use corporate_credit_balance.
whenToUse: when did we last buy credits
what have we spent credits on
whenNotToUse: Not for the current balance — that is corporate_credit_balance.
Not for candidates — use list_candidates.

entry_type.description: Restrict to credits added or credits used. Leave unset for both.

functions.sqlTemplate:
SELECT DISTINCT ON (cl.id)
       cl.created_at AS entry_date,
       cl.ledger_type AS entry_type,
       cl.credit_delta AS credits,
       cl.reason,
       cl.per_credit_cost,
       cl.total_amount,
       cl.payment_status,
       cl.paid_on
  FROM corporate_credit_ledger cl
 WHERE (cast({{param:entry_type}} AS text) IS NULL OR cl.ledger_type = {{param:entry_type}})
   AND {{scope:corporate_account_id}}
 ORDER BY cl.id DESC

functions.name: platform_level_throughput
functions.description: Administrator view of how much assessment has been completed at each level over a recent window, across every company: completions, distinct people, average score where the level has one, and the average minutes taken. Use for platform health and capacity.
whenToUse: how many assessments were completed at each level this month
how long does level 2 take on average
how many people finished level 3 in the last 90 days
whenNotToUse: Not scoped to one company — for that use level_completion_funnel as that company.
Not for session status overall — that is platform_assessment_overview.
Available to administrators only.

days.description: How far back to look, in days. Defaults to 30.

functions.sqlTemplate:
SELECT l.level_number,
       l.name AS level,
       l.pattern_type AS measures,
       count(DISTINCT a.id) AS completed,
       count(DISTINCT a.user_id) AS people,
       round(avg(a.total_score), 1) AS average_score,
       round(avg(extract(epoch FROM a.completed_at - a.started_at) / 60), 1) AS average_minutes
  FROM assessment_attempts a
  JOIN assessment_levels l ON l.id = a.assessment_level_id
 WHERE a.status = 'COMPLETED'
   AND a.completed_at >= now() - make_interval(days => coalesce({{param:days}}::int, 30))
 GROUP BY l.level_number, l.name, l.pattern_type, l.sort_order
 ORDER BY l.sort_order

functions.name: generate_my_report
functions.description: For the signed-in student: prepare their assessment report and hand back a download link. Takes a little while — the report is rendered in the background and the link arrives when it is ready. Only ever produces the caller's own report.
whenToUse: can I get a copy of my assessment report
whenNotToUse: Not for checking whether a report already exists — that is my_report.
Not for scores — those are my_level_scores.
Only ever produces the caller's own report.

report_type.description: Which report to produce. Leave unset for the standard full report.

precondition.sqlTemplate: SELECT 1 FROM registrations r WHERE r.is_deleted IS NOT TRUE AND {{scope:user_id}}
precondition.denyMessage: I could not find a registration for you, so there is no report to prepare.

functions.name: generate_candidate_report
functions.description: Prepare a candidate's assessment report and hand back a download link. Takes the candidate's user id, which find_candidate returns — look the person up by name first. The report is rendered in the background and the link arrives when it is ready. Only candidates in your own company can be generated for.
whenToUse: download the report for Priya Sharma
generate a report for this candidate
whenNotToUse: Not for checking whether a report is ready — find_candidate already says so.
Not for a whole cohort at once.
Look the candidate up by name first; this takes the id that lookup returns.

user_id.description: The candidate's user id, as returned by find_candidate. Never guess this — look the candidate up by name first.

report_type.description: Which report to produce. Leave unset for the standard full report.

precondition.sqlTemplate: SELECT 1 FROM registrations r WHERE r.user_id = {{param:user_id}} AND r.is_deleted IS NOT TRUE AND {{scope:corporate_account_id}}
precondition.denyMessage: That candidate is not in your account.
